subject: Agriculture
title: The Aswan High Dam
description: A quick, practical guide to The Aswan High Dam.

hook.text: Egypt's Aswan High Dam ended 5,000 years of Nile flooding. It was a triumph—and a problem.

buildup.text: Built in 1970, the dam stores a full year of Nile flow in Lake Nasser, providing year-round irrigation.

discovery.text: Farmers got reliable water and switched to multiple harvests per year. Agricultural output soared.

twist.text: Without annual silt deposits, farmland needs synthetic fertilizer. The dam stopped nature's free soil enrichment.

climax.text: The Nile Delta is sinking and eroding without new sediment. Egypt trades one crisis for another.

punchline.text: Control the river, lose its gifts. Every dam has a hidden bill.

quiz.question: What negative effect did the Aswan High Dam have on Egyptian farming?
options: It stopped annual silt deposits that naturally fertilized farmland

details.summary: The Aswan High Dam, completed in 1970, controls the Nile's annual flood and provides irrigation for Egyptian agriculture year-round. This topic covers the dam's enormous benefits, its unintended consequences for downstream agriculture, and the geopolitical tensions it created.
details.whyItMatters: The dam ended the Nile's natural flood cycle that had sustained Egyptian farming for 5,000 years, requiring chemical fertilizers to replace lost silt and creating new challenges for the Nile Delta's fertile land.
takeaways: The dam provides year-round irrigation to 3.3 million hectares of Egyptian farmland
Trapping silt behind the dam ended the natural fertilization of downstream farmland
The Nile Delta is eroding because sediment no longer replenishes its coastline

faq.question: What benefits did the Aswan High Dam bring to Egyptian agriculture?
faq.answer: The dam ended destructive floods, allowed year-round irrigation instead of seasonal farming, enabled multiple harvests per year, expanded cultivated area, and generated hydroelectric power that modernized Egypt's economy.

faq.question: What are the negative consequences of the Aswan High Dam?
faq.answer: The dam traps nutrient-rich silt in Lake Nasser, forcing farmers to use chemical fertilizers. The Nile Delta is eroding without sediment replenishment, waterlogging and salinization have increased, and downstream fisheries declined.
